title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Delivery Date, Decision Standard and Cover Expiry
content:
The delivery of the covered cargo is the reference point for the claim periods of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, and it also governs how long a cover remains able to take claims.

## Delivery date

Delivery is entered on the records at the point where the line releases the transport document and the cargo departs from the terminal. The date so recorded becomes the cover's delivery date. All notice periods and the claim time bar are counted from that date.

## Expiry of a cover

- The system expires a cover that has no open claim once the tier's time bar period has run from the delivery date. A cover in the active status and a cover showing a closed claim both expire in this way.
- Expiry ends a cover's capacity to receive claims.
- An open claim holds off expiry for as long as it awaits its decision.

## Service standard for decisions

Claims are decided within the tier's decision standard, counted from the date the documents become complete. The figure is a service standard.

| Tier | Decision standard after documents are complete (days) |
|---|---|
| `AHL Standard Carrier Liability` | 30 |
| `AHL Declared Value Liability` | 30 |
| `AHL CargoCare Essential` | 21 |
| `AHL CargoCare Plus` | 14 |
| `AHL CargoCare Premium` | 10 |
| `AHL CargoCare Total` | 7 |

## Points of judgement

| Cover's position when its time bar period has run | Outcome |
|---|---|
| active, no claim ever lodged | expires |
| claim closed, no claim open | expires |
| claim open, awaiting decision | no expiry while the claim awaits its decision |
